plan.activation_condition: Observable when cyclin excursions reach a moderate-to-high regime where the removal machinery is plausibly load-limited, while A remains appreciably above zero so degradation contributes materially to dC_dt; not distinguishable when C stays uniformly low or A is near zero.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: The same trajectories used for training already contain low- and higher-cyclin phases; the refinement changes the dC_dt-versus-C curvature within those phases and extends most clearly to holdout segments with larger cyclin peaks at similar A.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of a very large cyclin-removal saturation scale, the saturating loss law reduces to the parent bilinear degradation term.
plan.gap_statement: The current target law assumes regulator-mediated cyclin destruction increases indefinitely in direct proportion to cyclin concentration at fixed regulator activity.
plan.baseline_assumption: Active-regulator-mediated cyclin degradation is idealized as unsaturated mass action with respect to cyclin over the full observed range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Proteolytic destruction capacity is finite, so once active degradation machinery is engaged, additional cyclin cannot accelerate removal proportionally without bound.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent’s unsaturated degradation assumption rather than adding a new pathway. The parent response shortcut is a single-gain dependence of cyclin loss on C at fixed A: one slope, -k_cyclin_degradation*A, applies across the full cyclin range. In cell-cycle control, ubiquitin/proteolysis capacity can become effectively saturated when cyclin rises, making removal sublinear at high substrate load. The concrete distinguishing condition is to compare portions of trajectories with similar intermediate A but different C amplitudes, holding all fixed parameters shared across conditions. The parent predicts proportional extra loss as C increases, whereas the child predicts diminishing incremental loss at larger C, producing altered curvature in dC_dt versus C and typically higher or broader cyclin peaks before regulator-driven decline. This is observable under the actual protocol because C and A are both modeled states along the same trajectory; no unsampled intervention is required. The effect is scientifically admissible only when cyclin reaches a range where proteolytic throughput is challenged; if all observed C values are low, a refit of parent parameters could mask the difference and the refinement would be weak.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when regulator activation changes appreciably over a timescale comparable to downstream proteolytic engagement, especially for cyclin excursions through and above K_cyclin_activation while C is also near or above K_cyclin_degradation_saturation so delayed capacity affects peak loss.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as a modest lag between A rise and effective cyclin removal near pulse onset; in holdout, larger-amplitude or faster pulses amplify the same lag into clearer peak overshoot and delayed decay at comparable observed A.
plan.continuation_path: Take the maturation timescale to zero so effective degradation capacity instantaneously tracks A, recovering the parent degradation law.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuine delay in converting regulator activation into proteolytic destruction capacity cannot be represented by refitting fixed coefficients in an instantaneous two-state mapping; one additional dynamical state is needed to store the lagged capacity.
plan.gap_statement: The model treats active regulator fraction as if it immediately equals effective cyclin-destruction capacity, omitting finite assembly or engagement time of the degradation machinery after activation.
plan.baseline_assumption: Regulator activation and cyclin destruction are assumed to be in the same instantaneous phase, with no maturation delay between signaling activity and realized proteolytic capacity.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Activated degradation regulator often requires downstream complex assembly, substrate recruitment, or processive proteolytic engagement before full cyclin destruction capacity is realized.
plan.rationale: Vary the observed point along oscillatory trajectories so that comparable current C and A values are encountered on the rising versus falling sides of cyclin pulses, while holding the background conditions and all initial-condition conventions fixed. In the parent, dC_dt at a given C and A is identical regardless of recent history because A directly sets degradation strength. A child with finite maturation of degradation capacity changes the scored target mapping itself: at the same supplied C and A, dC_dt becomes less negative on the upswing before capacity has accumulated and more negative on the downswing after capacity has engaged. This is scientifically admissible when activation is not infinitely fast relative to destruction engagement; if maturation were extremely fast, the effect would collapse back to the parent and may be unresolvable.

plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption of one fixed cyclin saturation constant in the degradation term. Under admissible oscillatory trajectories starting from the stated nonzero initial conditions, D naturally varies through the cycle. The child then predicts that two phases with similar C but different D show different local slope/curvature of dC_dt versus C, whereas the parent can only produce proportional vertical rescaling by D with one fixed curvature. This is a genuine target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory change, because D is already a supplied state in the solver and enters the scored dC_dt directly. Limitation: if observed data never sample intermediate C while D varies appreciably, the refinement becomes difficult to identify.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when C reaches at least the baseline degradation saturation scale and D sweeps from low to moderate values during a pulse, so capacity maturation is engaged but not yet fully saturated.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest D mainly changes the onset of net cyclin decline; in holdout trajectories that climb to higher D within the same initial-condition protocol, the stronger mid-range curvature in the D-to-dC_dt map becomes visible as a sharper late collapse of cyclin.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added cooperativity/shape modification of destruction-capacity effectiveness to its linear limit, so effective degradation becomes proportional to D again.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes that once destruction capacity has matured into D, each increment of D contributes linearly to cyclin removal apart from Michaelis saturation in C, ignoring multicomponent assembly or multi-ubiquitylation/processivity thresholds in the effective action of the mature machinery.
plan.baseline_assumption: Matured degradation capacity D acts on cyclin with a single-phase linear efficacy in the numerator of the degradation term.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Fully matured cyclin destruction often still requires cooperative engagement of multiple proteolytic or substrate-recruitment steps, making low levels of D less effective and producing a sharper increase in removal only after sufficient mature capacity accumulates.
plan.rationale: Vary the observed trajectory segment through cycles so that C and D co-evolve from low to moderate-high values under the fixed initial conditions and constant synthesis background; hold all external conditions fixed as already assumed. In the parent, once A has created some D, the scored mapping from observed states to dC_dt has a single-phase dependence on D: increasing D immediately and fairly smoothly increases degradation at any given C, with only saturation effects. A more realistic refinement is that mature destruction capacity must itself engage cooperatively before it becomes fully productive, changing the target mapping rather than only auxiliary dynamics because dC_dt depends directly on the altered D efficacy. Then two states with similar C but different moderate D show a stronger curvature contrast: low D has less effect than the parent allows, whereas intermediate-to-high D produces a steeper increase in cyclin loss. This is admissible in the existing observation protocol because D is already an observed state in the joint trajectory, and the effect appears during normal oscillatory rises and falls without new interventions. A single refit of the parent parameters can shift overall gain or saturation scale, but it cannot simultaneously preserve weak early sensitivity to D and stronger mid-range sensitivity to D across the same trajectory family when its D action is constrained to be single-phase linear in the numerator.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when D is intermediate to high and A varies appreciably along the oscillation, especially during activation-relaxation lag where mature capacity persists while A has already declined or is still rising; negligible when A closely tracks D or D remains near zero.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within ordinary oscillatory traces from the stated initial conditions, the same D level is encountered on different phases with different A; training sees modest separation and holdout extends it to stronger pulses where A-D lag is larger.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where active engagement is always saturated or effectively proportional to a constant, so the added A dependence collapses to a fixed factor absorbed into k_cyclin_degradation.
contract.domain_mechanism: joint dependence of cyclin proteolysis on matured destruction capacity and contemporaneous active-regulator engagement
contract.scientific_mechanism: Even after assembly/maturation of destruction machinery, catalytic substrate processing commonly still requires active regulator occupancy or phosphorylation-dependent engagement, so mature capacity and active engagement jointly determine effective cyclin removal.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient correction because the target law changes from a single-valued mapping in (C,D) to a phase-sensitive mapping in (C,D,A), producing separable trajectory branches at matched C and D that cannot be created by globally retuning the parent constants.
contract.assumption_before: Once destruction capacity has matured into D, cyclin degradation is independent of the contemporaneous active regulator fraction A except through A's past effect on D.
contract.assumption_after: Matured destruction capacity D provides potential throughput, but actual cyclin degradation also requires contemporaneous active-regulator engagement through A.
contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when A/(K_degradation_capacity_activation + A) is effectively constant over the observed regime, especially in the active-engagement-saturated limit A >> K_degradation_capacity_activation, so the extra factor is absorbed into k_cyclin_degradation.
contract.observable_signature: Holding C and D fixed along sampled oscillatory trajectories, dC_dt becomes more negative for larger A. The effect is visible during phases where the same D is visited while A differs, notably on the rising versus relaxing sides of a cyclin pulse for intermediate or high D.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because the parent target mapping is exactly single-valued in C and D alone. Refitting k_cyclin_degradation, K_cyclin_degradation_saturation, or K_degradation_capacity_activation can only reshape that common surface, not split matched-(C,D) observations into systematically different dC_dt values according to A.
